messages.subject: when to use geom_rect(ymin=-Inf, ymax=Inf)
parts:
Dear all,

I'm trying to add a background band to a faceted plot with free
scales, and I'd just like to confirm whether using geom_rect(ymin=-
Inf, ymax=Inf) is the correct behavior.

Example code:

library(ggplot2)

## example data.frame
dates <- as.Date(paste(seq(1860,1870),'-01-01',sep=''))

d <- data.frame(
year=rep(dates,2),
facet.by=c(rep('a',11),rep('b',11)),
value=c(rnorm(11),rnorm(11)*100)
)

## recessions
recession <- data.frame(
start=as.Date('1865-01-01'),
end=as.Date('1867-01-01')
)

p <- ggplot(d, aes(year, value)) + geom_line()

p <- p + facet_wrap(~facet.by, scales='free', ncol=1)

p + geom_rect(aes(xmin=start, xmax=end, ymin=-Inf, ymax=Inf, x=NULL,
y=NULL), data=recession, fill='grey80', alpha=0.5)

This works as I expected to, but I'd just like to know whether there
are any pitfalls in setting ymin=-Inf and ymax=Inf. (an alternative
I've seen is to set them to the max and min of the dataset, but then
the panels end up having the same scales, I guess because they each
have a geom_rect with the same size).

Best regards,

Alexander
